exercises.title: Insert, search, height
exercises.task: Read Insert and Search. Run builds the tree 4 6 7 5 2 1 3, counts the nodes each search visits (the idea you had when you first wrote it), then compares the height of 1 000 keys inserted in random order with 1 000 keys inserted already sorted.

exercises.title: Write Insert
exercises.task: Fill Insert. It returns the root of the subtree after insertion, so the parent can reconnect itself with n.Left = Insert(n.Left, key): no parent pointers needed.
hints: Base case: an empty subtree (n == nil) becomes a new node.
Otherwise go left if the key is smaller, right if larger, and assign the result back to that side.
A key that is already there: return n unchanged (no duplicates).

exercises.title: Floor: which geological period
exercises.task: The geological periods are kept in a BST keyed by the time they began, in millions of years from today (negative: in the past). Which period was the Earth in at time t? That is the floor: the largest key ≤ t. Follow one path from the root, like Search, remembering the best candidate.
hints: If the node's key is ≤ t, it is a candidate; a better one can only be on its right.
If the node's key is > t, the answer can only be on its left.
A loop is enough: for n != nil { … }, keeping best and found.
